verdicts.strongest_argument: Same event, same document, and the same self-refutation as the WLY version: the quoted headline states 'HPE, WLY Also Gain On Joining Federal AI Initiative', so the market marked Wiley up on 2026-07-22, and the item is published in the admissible stored body (docs/d7ff82564a557ffced5d936a6aa2bd1f37a02219.txt in the WLY capture, entry 2026-07-22T17:19:31Z). The finding's window is also wrong for its test - the twenty sessions ending 09-02 begin in early August, after the event, so the -6.3% and -2.5% figures cannot measure how 22 July was received. Then there is the class-B argument, which I think defeats the finding rather than rescuing it. The hunter says the class B stays unpriced because 'at 247 shares a day the class B does not reprice on information until someone needs to trade it'. That is true and it is precisely why this cannot be an edge: the baseline shows a median absolute print reaction of 1.98% with two recorded readings of exactly 0.00%, a deadband floored at 1.5%, and avg_volume_20d of 247 shares. A share class that does not move on its own earnings, on volume of a few hundred shares, cannot express a re-rating; a claim that information is unpriced in an instrument that cannot price anything is a statement about market structure, not an edge, and it is structural and known to anyone who has looked at the quote. Any ranking of WLYB on this basis is a ranking of an untradeable series.

The class B is within 3.3% of its 52-week high and up 79% from its low, so whatever re-rating the AI thesis warranted has largely happened.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Nothing about the information; only a change in the class-B liquidity, since at 247 shares a day the instrument cannot express a view either way.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the identical claim to WLY#1, drawn from the identical index for the identical CIK, and the hunter says outright 'do not count it twice across the two tickers'. My verdict is therefore the same: reachable but unconnected, and probably empty. The 8-K carries item 9.01, meaning an exhibit and so a press release, which indicates public dissemination in July; seven Form 4s on one day is a grant or vesting event across an officer group rather than seven arrivals, with a single Form 3 marking the one genuinely new insider; and no body, share count or officer name is stored anywhere in either capture. The rebasing mechanism is generic, unsized and of indeterminate sign, and it is signed against the finding above. On this share class the point is doubly moot: with a 1.98% median reaction and 247 shares a day of volume, a governance item cannot be expressed in the price at all.

interactions: Both WLYB findings are the same claims as WLY#0 and WLY#1, on the same company, the same CIK, the same document and the same print; the hunter states this deliberately and asks that they not be double-counted. My numbers are aligned with the WLY verdicts, with WLYB#0 scored slightly higher because the class-B liquidity argument the hunter offers as the reason it is unpriced is also the reason it cannot be traded.
